subject: Throughput acceptance checks and test plan for AtlasAI RFP
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlasai.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlasai.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasAI RFP - clarifications on throughput acceptance

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the RFP reply. A couple of quick clarifications on the performance section so we can align our procurement acceptance criteria:

- Target production profile: 120k requests/day, 95th percentile request size ~350 tokens, median ~120 tokens.
- Peak concurrency expected: sustained bursts to 550 concurrent streams for up to 30 minutes (twice/day).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for short single-turn prompts (~120 tokens) and <= 1s for median prompts with streaming acceptable.
- Throughput acceptance: we need a documented test run showing 24-hour soak at scaled load (or synthetic equivalent) and a burst run reproducing the peak concurrency with fallbacks.

Can Redwood provide the exact test methodology you’ll use (traffic shaping, model variants, quantization profiles), the environment (hosted vs dedicated), and the artifacts you’ll produce as evidence (raw traces, token breakdown, cost/per-token metrics)? Also call out any differences we should expect between hosted API and a Dedicated deployment for the same workload.

We have an external load consultancy (LoadLab) on standby — cc'd — who will coordinate the synthetic driver.

Appreciate a short reply today if possible; procurement wants to list the acceptance tests in the contract.

Regards,
Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
AtlasAI
From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlasai.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasai.com, pm@loadlab.io
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasAI RFP - clarifications on throughput acceptance

Hi Jordan — thanks, this is clear and helpful.

Short answer: yes, we can produce a repeatable acceptance bundle that includes the items you listed. Attached is a draft test plan (redwood-atlasai-testplan-v1.xlsx) that outlines the test phases, data collection points, and pass/fail criteria. Key highlights:

- Environment: initial runs on Redwood Hosted with a dedicated routing policy (isolated pool) to match production. If you proceed with Redwood Dedicated we will run the same test matrix on your reserved pool; results are comparable when config-matched (we document any kernel/quantization deltas).
- Model variants: we’ll run both the curated 13B float and a 13B int8 quantized variant; acceptance requires the float baseline plus a documented performance/cost delta for quantized variant.
- Traffic shaping: driver will replay a 24-hour synthesized trace (derived from the profile you provided) plus three scheduled 30-minute peak bursts to 550 streams.
- Metrics captured: token-level latency distribution, server-side queue time, CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate, and per-request fallback events.
- Artifact bundle: aggregated lat/throughput CSVs, annotated latency traces, sample raw request/response (sanitized), cost-per-token breakdown, and a short runbook describing how to reproduce the test in Dedicated.

Next steps proposed:
1) You confirm the exact token-size distribution for the 24-hour trace (attached sheet has our assumed distribution).
2) Approve a 2-hour scheduling window for the initial proof run next week (we recommend Tue 10/13 02:00–04:00 PT).
3) Confirm whether you want us to run on Hosted isolated pool (default) or provide access to a Dedicated pool for the first-run equivalence test.

I’ve looped in Ben, Marissa and Karthik internally to finalize the test matrix and provide the annotated evidence set. If LoadLab wants to run a pre-warm driver we’ll coordinate ports/IPs and TLS cert exchange.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priya — quick pass attached (throughput-matrix.csv). Main notes:

- We should run the 24-hour soak on a single isolated host-group equivalent to their per-instance capacity and then scale to N=8 replicas to validate network/replica coordination and KV-cache behavior. That gives us both per-replica throughput and system-wide throughput.
- For 95th percentile latency at ~120 tokens, we see the greatest sensitivity to batching window and kernel selection — recommend we test batch windows {5, 10, 25ms} and record P95 across each.
- Quantized variant: measure both int8 runtime and the int8+KV cache disabled to surface fallback penalties; include a simple regression test that replays any fallback-causing prompts at 1x and 10x frequency to confirm correct degradation handling.
- Sample logs: I attached an annotated example 'sample-latency-logs-annotated.txt' showing trace format and expected fields (ts, req_id, server_q, gpu_ms, tokens_out).

I’ll add a short appendix explaining how results map to cost-per-token calculations for procurement to digest.

-Ben
Engineering Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference
